timeline.title: Symptoms intensify, seizure risk climbs
symptoms: Increased sensitivity to sound, light and touch
Rising seizure risk, peaking near the 24 hour mark

timeline.title: Highest seizure risk, hallucinations may start
symptoms: Most alcohol withdrawal seizures happen in this window
Seeing, hearing or feeling things that are not there
Fast heartbeat and high blood pressure

timeline.title: Delirium tremens can begin
symptoms: Confusion and disorientation about time, place or person
Sharp rises in heart rate, breathing rate and blood pressure

timeline.title: Delirium tremens can continue; most symptoms fade
symptoms: Delirium tremens, once present, usually continues for several more days and is a medical emergency
Most other withdrawal symptoms ease over the following days
Sleep problems and anxiety can persist for weeks in heavy drinkers

erNow: A seizure, or convulsions of any kind
Confusion: not knowing what day it is, or not recognising where you are
Seeing, hearing, or feeling things that are not there
Unusual restlessness, irritability, or agitation that will not settle
A heartbeat that is very fast or irregular, or blood pressure that spikes or drops sharply
Abdominal pain, or vomiting or passing blood
highRisk: You are at higher risk of severe withdrawal, including seizures and delirium tremens, if you have had a withdrawal seizure or delirium tremens before, if you have been hospitalised for withdrawal more than once, or if you have liver disease or a liver transplant. Tell emergency staff this history.
closing: Alcohol withdrawal can be treated. Treatment is safe. Call now.
